summary: On node1, created datauser and a dedicated XFS filesystem (loopback image /var/lib/srv-data-backing/data.img, 512M) mounted at /srv/data via /etc/fstab with usrquota. Set a kernel-enforced XFS user quota of 100MB (bsoft=bhard=100m) for datauser. Verified enforcement: 60MB write succeeds, 150MB write is hard-blocked by the filesystem with EDQUOT at exactly 100MB used. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id, issued a graceful reboot, polled until the node returned, confirmed boot_id changed (1e0cb179... -> 973e294e...), and re-verified post-restart that the fstab mount, datauser account, and quota enforcement all recovered correctly (repeated the 150MB write test post-reboot, again blocked at 100MB).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/filesystem baseline (Ubuntu 24.04, ext4 root, no /srv/data, no datauser, xfsprogs already installed)
Created 512M loopback-backed XFS filesystem image and formatted with mkfs.xfs
Added persistent /etc/fstab entry mounting the image at /srv/data with usrquota,prjquota options
Set XFS user quota for datauser: bsoft=bhard=100m via xfs_quota
Functionally verified quota: 60MB write succeeded, 150MB write blocked by kernel with 'Disk quota exceeded' at 100MB used, cleaned up test files
Captured pre-restart boot_id, mount state, quota config, and datauser identity as baseline
Issued native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, confirming genuine reboot
Re-verified post-restart: fstab mount active, quota config intact (Enforcement: ON), datauser present, and repeated 150MB write test again blocked at 100MB by filesystem quota

evidence.requirement: Baseline: /srv/data, datauser, and node1 filesystem state before changes
evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing datauser or /srv/data, ext4 root with no quota support, xfsprogs already installed

evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself
evidence.summary: Created datauser, built dedicated XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, set bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota, and demonstrated kernel-level enforcement: 60MB write succeeded, 150MB write was hard-blocked by XFS with 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly 100MB used, then cleaned up leaving quota at 0/100M

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline capture on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, active /srv/data mount, quota config (datauser 0/100M), fstab entry, and datauser account presence prior to restart
Issued native 'shutdown -r now'; command acknowledgement returned (stream closed) before the node disconnected, confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart polling and availability recovery
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down/rebooting), second poll succeeded with a fresh uptime, confirming exec access returned after restart

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery for node1
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 973e294e-ea59-4f62-8a8a-a60c5071b1c2 differs from pre-restart value, proving a genuine reboot occurred. Verified /srv/data fstab mount, datauser account, and XFS quota (Enforcement: ON, 100M soft/hard) all recovered automatically, and re-ran the 150MB write test which was again blocked at exactly 100MB by the filesystem, confirming enforcement survives restart
